proof:
Every cube vertex is exposed in the complete base hull. At any mark, a nonvertical ambient cap captures at least its own ramp mass. Conversely, for each continuous direction a large finite exposing tilt makes the other bounded fiber margins fall below the ramp support without changing the own margin. Pure-base caps include the whole own fiber. Thus mixed depth on each fiber equals its own smoothed depth. For a fixed continuous direction the through-mark buffered threshold is convex in the mark by concavity of the tied profile (32418f8d50e792af). The mass is nonincreasing in threshold, so the depth superlevel sets are convex; affine barycentric symmetries preserve the own volume, the covariance norm under the dual action, and the tied profile. The orbit average is $y$, making it a deepest mark. Over $\Gamma(u)=1$ the own ramp integral is continuous on a compact set, so its minimizing direction exists. The centroid lower bound at width zero is 6769574fc1bd9f8d at full mass, with equality from any centroid vertex cap, of fraction $\gamma_d$. The outward buffered ramp dominates that ordinary infimum. Applying a fixed ordinary minimizing direction and dominated convergence supplies the reverse limit. Thus at small parameters $Q_{\varepsilon,\delta}<V$, so the nonvertical minimized profile is genuinely active. Its positive-coarea strip is in the own fiber for small widths, and its base centroid is exactly $p$.

By d90ba05577427854, the optimum at the centroid has denominator one and energy $V$, while every energy in each real fiber is at most $V$. Fiber volume is constant. Thus in df51254e978fb6a2 both affine upper supports can be constant, and their normalized combination is $R=1$. The field on every marked fiber is therefore $h_y(n)$, of total cost $NdV$ by the flux of $x-y$. For any isolated minimizing cap let $q=(u\cdot(x-y)+\varepsilon f(Y)\Gamma(u))/(\delta\Gamma(u))$ on its own fiber. The divergence theorem applied to the Lipschitz field $(x-y)\Psi(q)$ gives
$
\int_{\partial D}h_y(n)\Psi(q)\,dS=dQ_{\varepsilon,\delta}
 +\int_D\frac{\Psi'(q)}{\delta\Gamma(u)}\,u\cdot(x-y)\,dx
 \le dQ_{\varepsilon,\delta}.
$
On the support of $\Psi'$, $u\cdot(x-y)$ is nonpositive because the ramp and buffer are outward. Other fibers contribute nothing to the numerator by the strict finite tilt. The ratio bound, limit, and strict gap from $\gamma_d$ follow for $N\ge2$. This uses actual old active profiles and the unlocalized field, without requiring the product to minimize the smoothed body objective.

statement: Let $n,d\ge1$, $D$ be a $d$-simplex of volume $V$ and centroid $y$, and let $C=[0,1]^n\times D$ with $N=2^n$ sampled fibers. Use the uniform outward ramp with positive width $\delta$, nonnegative tied buffer $\varepsilon f$, and the pooled covariance norm $\Gamma$. For sufficiently small $\varepsilon,\delta>0$, every base has an actual deepest mark at $y$; an attaining nonvertical cap can be chosen at any one source so that all other fiber profiles are identically zero by a finite tilt. Its smooth own mass is $Q_{\varepsilon,\delta}$. The canonical common chart at that source may be chosen $R=1$, with associated field $h_y(n)=h_D(n)-n\cdot y$ on every fiber. Its normalized payment for the isolated cap (or any probability menu of such caps) is at most $Q_{\varepsilon,\delta}/(NV)$, with $Q_{\varepsilon,\delta}/(NV)\to\gamma_d/N$ as $\varepsilon,\delta\downarrow0$. Thus this field does not give the individual fraction $\gamma_d$ for small positive parameters.
title: The unlocalized canonical chart loses individual payment on an actual product
